comments.content: You can handle this project after #55 is complete.

Using the open ai playground helped me rapidly iterate and improve the results by easily being able to adjust the prompt and test, so I highly recommend using that for prompt development. 
The first attempt I think I might have spent at least a couple hours on the prompting alone.

I realize that pull request review comments should be `relevance: 1` always. They definitely don't make sense out of the context of its associated code sample. 
Eventually it would be great to score pull request review comment relevance in a different manner, where we can feed the code sample to ChatGPT and provide it a new prompt, such as, "is this a valuable pull request reviewer comment for the following code snippet?"
https://github.com/ubiquity/ts-template/issues/50#issuecomment-2186008265
It seems fine although to be honest sometimes it's a bit difficult to tell what's going on from our results table, especially from mobile.
That doesn't seem right.

I think include the specification because as a human reviewer sometimes (but not always) I review the spec when looking at some of the changes. Maybe this is 1 out of 10 times but if I'm confused on why certain changes are made then I review the spec. I think it's a good idea to give the LLM the additional context if it's needed if it is cheap to do so.

I'm not sure what the right answer is but I feel like maybe one more prompt could be the solution. We just need to provide the spec, full diff, the full pull conversation, and then ask if it's a useful comment I think.

As a human manager I feel that I would take all of this into context to determine how useful somebody's comment is, that's why I suggested these elements.  
Let's send empty diffHunk then.
I think the rule is pascal case and technically it's pascal case.

Honestly it's a bit difficult to understand results in detail especially from mobile but if you think that it looks as expected we can merge. 
I'm a bit confused why many are scored zero
Interesting point. If relevance evaluation was skipped due to the config, then - makes sense. If it evaluated to 0 then we should write 0. Let's do this.
@gentlementlegen change the package version to `*` to waste less time on housekeeping
@EresDev Solve merge conflict and you can merge
Looks like there's a ton of changes. Perhaps you should ensure it works by posting QA

I am not sure if that makes sense. The idea was the pull-request comments are related to the code itself, and not to the specification which is why we put the relevance to `1` in the first place, because these comments are unrelated.
@0x4007 maybe the comments for the pull-request should be checked against the code block they are commenting, or something related to code anyway? I also usually like to specify in the pull-request what are the changes implied which also could be used instead of the specification.
Is it okay to change? I think the mocks return `/comment-incentives/issues/22` API responses.

If they are added back to the configuration via the file, will they override anything? If these options are not available at all anymore, it would be great to remove them from the codebase too, otherwise ignore my comment.
Shouldn't this be spotted by `eslint`?
If that was the case then the linter would detect `commentsToEvaluate` as wrong. Either it accepts both, either there is no rule for this.
